page: Amazon Web Services m8a.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the AMD EPYC 9R45 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core topology, avoiding thread contention from simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation stands at 128 GB of high-speed DDR5 operating at 6 GHz, sustaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The instance provisions a 15 Gbps baseline network link, while omitting local instance storage and discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong general compute and memory subsystems. In single-core tests, the platform reaches top-decile performance with a Geekbench score of 2,816 and stress-ng throughput of 3,777.48. Multi-core compute performance remains in the upper quartile with a Geekbench multi-core result of 28,042 and a PassMark CPU rating of 79,557.66. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers 213.23 GB/sec in large uncached reads and 136.6 GB/sec in uncached writes. Database handling capabilities are pronounced, achieving top-tier ratings in PassMark database operations (40,843.98) and sustaining over 106.65 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware support for AVX-512 extensions, including VNNI and BF16, aids vectorized math and small-scale CPU machine learning inference, delivering 378.79 tokens per second on lightweight 135M parameter models.

The lack of bundled local NVMe storage and dedicated hardware accelerators limits applicability for IO-intensive scratch disk workflows and large-scale deep learning model training. However, the dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores provide predictable latency and execution consistency across scale. The balanced resource density yields efficient utilization profiles for enterprise web applications, intermediate data caching, CI/CD compilation jobs, microservice clusters, and production database engines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration delivers 32 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, alongside 128 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage and discrete GPUs, utilizing network-attached storage alongside a 15 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate exceptional single-thread and multi-thread computational throughput, with Geekbench single-core reaching the top 10% and multi-core scoring 28,042. Memory bandwidth reaches 213.23 GB/sec for large-block reads, supporting strong in-memory operations as demonstrated by 106.65 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier database performance in PassMark testing. Supported instruction sets including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 also facilitate lightweight CPU-based machine learning inference. This instance fits enterprise database hosting, backend API services, compilation pipelines, and memory-coupled compute tasks.

tagline: High-frequency 32-core AMD EPYC architecture paired with high-speed DDR5 memory and AVX-512 capabilities for scalable compute and enterprise application workloads.
bullet_points: 32 dedicated AMD EPYC 9R45 physical cores operating at up to 4.5 GHz without hyperthreading
128 GB of high-speed DDR5 system memory (4 GB per core) clocked at 6 GHz
Hardware vector acceleration via AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16 instruction sets
15 Gbps baseline network throughput backed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture
Absence of integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes
Suited for mid-sized relational databases, caching layers, software compilation, and backend application servers
